title: Westpac grills its customers
full_text:
Westpac customers have been asked to reveal detailed personal information about their wealth, income, employment and finances, or risk restrictions being placed on their banking under a customer verification program.
The letters gave customers until August 31 to disclose everything from their employment status and occupation to the source of their income, wealth, tax residency and banking activities.
Some recipients initially believed the letters were a scam because they requested personal and financial data.
Westpac declined to reveal how many customers had received the notices and whether any accounts had been restricted.
A Westpac spokesman said the verification reflected banks’ obligations under Australia’s anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing laws. The Australian Banking Association chief executive Simon Birmingham said banks had to periodically verify identities under Australia’s anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing laws and urged concerned customers to contact the bank through official channels.
